title: Space

match.reason: The closest bank point, geo-place-space, teaches place and space together at Year 11 depth, while the new point covers only space for Year 7, so it is broader and at a different depth and needs a new card.

draft.title: Space
card: Space is about where things are and how they are spread out. Geographers ask where something is and why it is there.
Location
where something is, such as a town's position on a map or its distance from the coast.
Distance
how far apart two things are. Distance can affect how easily people reach services such as a hospital.
Pattern
the way things are spread out on a map. They may be clustered close together, spread out evenly, or in a line.
draft.remember: Space asks where things are, how far apart they are and what pattern they make.

a.q: A map shows most of a region's farms bunched close together near one river. Which part of space does this describe?
opts: A pattern, because the farms are clustered
A distance, because the farms are near a river
A place, because the farms are on the map
A location, because the farms are spread evenly
a.why: The way the farms are spread out is a pattern, and here they are clustered. Distance is about how far apart two things are, so it does not name the whole spread. The farms are not spread evenly.
a.clue: Think about how the farms are spread out, not one position.

b.q: Kai lives in a small town in the Northern Territory. The nearest hospital is 300 km away. Which idea from space helps explain why getting medical help is hard for him?
opts: Distance, because the hospital is far from his town
Pattern, because the towns form a line on the map
Place, because Kai values his town differently
Location, because his town has a name on the map
b.why: The hospital is a long way from Kai's town, so distance explains the difficulty. Pattern is about how many things are spread out, and this case has only one town and one hospital.

a.best: A pattern, because the farms are clustered

b.best: Distance, because the hospital is far from his town

problems.detail: The location example 'its distance from the coast' uses distance to explain location, though the next line teaches distance as its own idea. This blurs the two ideas the questions ask students to tell apart.
Why (b) says pattern is about 'how many things are spread out'. The card defines pattern as the way things are spread out, so this misstates it.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer: pattern for (a) and distance for (b). Minor issues: the card's location example ('distance from the coast') overlaps with distance, and why (b) misstates pattern as 'how many things are spread out'.
